history.gap: The left "schematic" column is a dead zone: the gold sparkline hugs the top, the dotted LATER rule sits 250px below with nothing between, and the caption "TWEE NIVEAUS, SCHEMATISCH" falls off the bottom of the viewport while the 09 TOEGANG hairline starts 40px right of the chart axis it should share. At the bar the diagram is sized to the copy column, the NU line and LATER line sit on the Gratis and Premium baselines so the graph literally is the two tiers, and the two CTA rules are the same length (they are 38px vs 25px now). history.motion: Restrained and coherent: rows fade up in sequence, the sparkline draws itself in over two frames, nav compacts on scroll; nothing overshoots.
history.verdict: A is a disciplined gold-on-charcoal editorial with real typographic hierarchy (italic Gratis against roman Premium, tracked small caps, hairline CTAs) let down by an under-designed chart column and a clipped caption. B has the more cinematic material but ships unreadable copy, a logo collision, a struck-through mobile nav and broken text animation, which no amount of fog forgives.

At the bar the figure is either redrawn as a proper full-width diagram with NU/LATER as inline labels tied to the two tiers, or dropped on mobile, and every caption obeys the same alignment as the column. Also reconsider the inverted hierarchy: the free tier is set small italic and the premium tier large roman for no legible reason.
history.motion: Orderly staggered fade-up of blocks with the sparkline drawing in — restrained and consistent, if a little generic.
history.verdict: A is a disciplined dark-and-gold editorial block with real typographic control (spaced caps, hairline buttons, a considered measure) let down by a decorative chart that breaks on mobile and an inverted tier hierarchy. B leans on beautiful stock-feeling photography while the actual design fails at the basics — illegible copy over the image, a label crashing into the logo, broken word spacing and a mobile dead zone — so A wins comfortably, though neither is shortlist-ready.

history.gap: The two tiers are thin, near-identical stacked modules (40px serif heading, two-line note, text link) with no price, no feature enumeration, and the whole left column from x300 to x570 is empty save one hairline, so on desktop the section reads as a well-set caption rather than a designed access moment. At the bar the tier names would carry real scale contrast against the caps labels, the NU/LATER timeline device would be extended into something that earns its width, and the link treatment would be consistent (KOM BINNEN gets an arrow, VOLG HET IN DE SERVER does not).
history.motion: Staggered fade-up of Gratis then Premium with a gold progress hairline at the foot — restrained and correctly sequenced, if unremarkable.
history.verdict: A has the louder idea (condensed grotesk slicing through a portrait image) but its craft fails at the basics: nav collisions, bleed-through on mobile, and a half-viewport dead zone under the logo grid. B is quieter and underbuilt as an access section, yet every hairline, label, and caps tracking is under control, and at SOTD level the site that makes no mistakes beats the site that makes visible ones.
